issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for Person.birthday across artifacts. The problem statement (UML and description) and the template common model declare Person.birthday as java.time.LocalDate, and the template client/view code (PersonScene) and template common Person class use LocalDate throughout. In the solution repository, the common Person model declares birthday as String. This creates two problems: (1) a cross-artifact inconsistency (solution differs from problem/template expectations), and (2) an internal inconsistency inside the solution repository where client code (PersonScene) and server logic (PersonService sorting by BIRTHDAY) still expect a LocalDate, which will cause compile-time/type errors or unexpected behavior. Students comparing template and solution or trying to run/adapt the solution will be confused and blocked by type mismatches and likely compilation failures.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Person.birthday type consistent across all artifacts. The least disruptive fix (and the one that matches the problem statement and template client code) is to change the solution repository's common Person.java to use java.time.LocalDate for the birthday field (and update getters/setters accordingly). Ensure any JSON serialization/deserialization configuration (if necessary) handles LocalDate consistently so client and server code compile and behave as intended. Alternatively, if String is preferred, update the problem statement, template Person model, and client/view code to use String consistently and document the expected date format — but prefer aligning the solution to the template (LocalDate) to preserve the intended exercise design.
